newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs condemn settlements, warn Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arabs condemn settlements, warn Israel.

text.p: The Arab League on Sunday condemned Israel's expansion of settlements on occupied Arab land and warned the Jewish state such practices could destroy the entire Middle East peace process.

"Israel is endangering the peace process with settlements, which are considered against international law and are totally rejected by Arab countries and the world community," Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid told a news conference.
He was speaking at the end of an emergency session of the 22-member league's council that was requested by the Palestinian Authority's mission and Syria to protest the settlement issue.
"We will never have peace of mind until the settlements issue is ended," Meguid added.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has infuriated Arabs by refusing to trade occupied Arab land for peace -- the basic principle of a 1991 Madrid Middle East peace conference -- and also by lifting a ban imposed by the former government on building Jewish settlements on these lands.
Even as the Arab League met, Netanyahu vowed on Sunday that the Jordan Valley area of the occupied West Bank would be part of Israel forever.

"The prime minister met today with representatives of the Jordan Valley...In the meeting the prime minister said that the government saw the Jordan Valley as inseparable from the State of Israel in any permanent agreement," Netanyahu's office said in a statement issued in Israel.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Sunday to complain about Israel's settlements policy and the failure of talks with Israel to resolve outstanding issues.
"Israel is trying to take land and to give us peace and security. There can never be security or peace without Palestinian land," said Mohammed Subeih, the PA's representative to the Arab League.
More than 130,000 Jews live amid nearly two million Palestinians in settlements among the self-rule areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
The issue was to be discussed at final status talks under an interim peace deal signed by Israel's previous government and the PLO in September 1993. The talks have yet to start under Netanyahu.
The Palestinian Authority warned Israel in a statement circulated at the emergency meeting that its policies would reignite violence in the region and alienate the Jewish state.

"Israel insists on ripping apart the West Bank to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state, but we are determined to defend our lands by all possible means against (Israeli) racist settlement plans," the statement said.

Abdel-Meguid said he would contact the United States and Russia -- the co-sponsors of the peace process, the European Union and foreign ministers of the Islamic Organisation Conference, who are due to meet in Indonesia this month, to convey Arab dismay at Israel's settlements policy.

Asked whether the Arab League had asked its member states to reconsider steps towards normalising relations with Israel -- as an Arab summit in June warned -- Abdel-Meguid said the league did not have the power to take such steps but would leave it to the leadership of each country.
